assumptions: Cases need fictional project states, a synthetic repository checkout and deterministic Search Console fakes; they are not measured model output or live integration evidence.
tests/test_site_architecture.py checks offline that the documented redirects.json block is what the technical fix reads.
cost_drivers: Codex input grows with the repository's routes and navigation, the audit, the snapshot and the previous report; output grows with URL and redirect rows, capped at 64000 bytes.
A plan calls Search Console up to five times; a follow-up fewer. Provider processing is unmeasured.
effects: Replaces reports/organic/site-architecture/SITE_ARCHITECTURE.md. Reads the repository without changing it. The technical fix later asks about each row in its redirects.json block; nothing here edits a page, redirect or PR.

cases.description: A Next.js repository with /features/* moving to /product/*, an existing /old-pricing redirect and eight clicked URLs. The plan retargets /old-pricing straight at /plans and asks about /features/whiteboard as a 410.
No planned change; the repository's header omits /pricing and the only link to it sits four clicks from home. The gate passes on click depth from the repository link graph.
About 60 routes, two integration pages, no audit, snapshot or Page decisions and no trigger: a clean stop with explicit unknowns.
A previous plan with a baseline but no applied_on input: the follow-up stops and asks for the date before any comparison.
Search Console page and date rows come back truncated during a URL change; the plan states incomplete coverage instead of false zeros.

rubric.question: Do routes, navigation links and click depth cite the repository path:line they come from, with client-only links marked not assessed?
Is every moved must-keep URL represented once, with no chain, no source that is also a target and no unrelated home redirect, and does the redirects.json block match the table?
Does every number name its window and source, with unknown kept apart from zero, and does the gate pass or stop only on supported evidence?
